---
title: "How do I find the probability above a threshold?"
---

## What the question asks

How do I find the probability above a threshold?

## Steps in RStudio

1. Check the mean, standard deviation, and threshold.

2. Call pnorm(threshold,mean,sd,lower.tail=FALSE).

3. Interpret the result as the upper-tail probability.

## Runnable example

```{r}
answer <- pnorm(120,mean=100,sd=15,lower.tail=FALSE)
print(answer)
```

## Interpret the result

The modeled probability above 120 is about 0.091, or 9.1%, for a normal distribution centered at 100 with standard deviation 15.

## Check before using your own data

Distinguish P(X > a) from P(X < a); the two areas add to 1 for a continuous normal model.
